newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy Dept backs pipeline safety bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy Dept backs pipeline safety bill.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department in a letter this week urged the White House to sign an oil and natural gas pipeline regulation bill, which several Democratic congressmen pressed President Clinton to veto.

But a memo from Deputy Energy Secretary Charles Curtis to the White House Office of Management and Budget endorsed the bill, saying the measure also had the backing of the Transportation Department's Office of Pipeline Safety.
Interstate Natural Gas Association of America, which released the Energy Department memo, also released letters signed by other 33 Democratic congressmen urging Clinton to sign the bill.
Clinton has until Monday to decide whether to sign the measure that makes regulators make more use of cost-benefit studies and risk analyses before imposing new rules.
Five Democratic congressmen who opposed the bill wrote Clinton to urge him to veto what they said amounted to a "pipeline deregulation bill."
The Energy Department memo said it was "aware of the criticism of this legislation by the environmental community..."

But it said, "A Presidential veto of the Accountable Pipeline Safety and Partnership Act would halt or significantly delay productive negotiations between the Congress, the Department of Transportation and the regulated community, resulting in the postponement of opportunities to improve environmental protection."
The Senate passed the industry-backed bill unanimously, while the House passed it 276-125.
